provenance.description: US macroeconomic summary moments used as calibration targets for the econ-sae simulator (Phase 10). Values are committed offline (no live API) for full reproducibility; refresh by re-deriving from the cited FRED series.

fred_series.GDPC1: Real Gross Domestic Product, quarterly, seasonally-adjusted annual rate
fred_series.FEDFUNDS: Effective Federal Funds Rate, monthly, percent (aggregated to quarterly)
fred_series.CPIAUCSL: CPI for All Urban Consumers: All Items, monthly index (aggregated to quarterly)
fred_series.GFDEBTN: Federal Debt: Total Public Debt, level (reference only)

provenance.frequency: one simulator period is treated as one calendar quarter
provenance.vintage: hand-entered 2026-05 from published FRED summary statistics over the window above
notes: Targets are scale-invariant (growth rates, volatilities, autocorrelation, an event frequency, a ratio). The simulator's GDP/money/price are in arbitrary synthetic units, so levels are never targeted.

recession_freq is the prevalence of the simulator's `phase:contraction` rule (GDP < 0.90 x trailing-5-period mean), set near the US recession share so the contraction regime label stays learnable (neither degenerate nor saturated). It is NOT the NBER recession rule applied verbatim.

debt_to_money is reference-only (weight 0): the simulator's household+firm debt/money ratio (~0.15) lives on a different absolute scale than US federal-debt/M2 (~0.85), so matching it would distort behavioral params without improving realism. Reported for transparency, excluded from the objective.
Pre-COVID window (ends 2019) avoids the 2020 outlier quarter dominating the volatility moments.
